bib.title: ChipNeMo: Domain-Adapted LLMs for Chip Design

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only (lines ~728-1093); figures not viewed, only captions in text

question: Can domain adaptation of LLaMA2 (tokenizer, continued pretraining, alignment, fine-tuned retriever) beat general LLMs including GPT-4 on industrial chip-design tasks?
hypothesis: Domain-adaptive pretraining plus alignment and domain RAG gives better in-domain performance than off-the-shelf LLMs at a small fraction of pretraining cost, without losing general ability.
contributions: Domain-adapted LLM effectiveness shown on three use cases: engineering assistant chatbot, EDA script generation, bug summarization and analysis
ChipNeMo models outperform vanilla LLMs on domain AutoEval benchmarks and human evaluations
SteerLM over traditional SFT improves chatbot human score by 0.62 on 7-point Likert
SFT on 1.4K domain instructions improves EDA script correctness by 18%
Domain-adaptive tokenization reduces domain token count by up to 3.3%
Fine-tuned retriever improves hit rate by 30% over a pre-trained retriever

method.summary: Four-stage adaptation of LLaMA2 7B/13B/70B: extend the tokenizer with ~9K domain tokens, continue pretraining (DAPT) on ~24B tokens of NVIDIA internal chip-design data plus ~9.2% public data, align with SFT or SteerLM on 128K/56K general plus 1.4K domain instructions, and fine-tune an e5-small retriever for RAG. Evaluated by multiple-choice AutoEval, human Likert ratings, and EDA script pass rates.
method.task: domain-adaptive continued pretraining, alignment and RAG for chip design

datasets.name: Internal chip design corpus (bug summaries, design source, documentation, verification, other)
datasets.size: 23.1B tokens after filtering (Table 3: 25.3B data tokens, 24.1B training tokens incl. public)

datasets.preprocessing: shell/Python collection, BeautifulSoup HTML stripping, line-count filter, checksum dedup, human vs tool-generated split; code downsampled, docs upsampled

datasets.name: Public mix-in (Wikipedia, GitHub)
datasets.source: Wikipedia from The Pile (Gao 2020); GitHub from The Stack (Kocetkov 2022)
datasets.preprocessing: sub-sampled, balanced natural language and code

datasets.name: General chat SFT data (OASST, FLAN, P3, small proprietary)
OASST for SteerLM
datasets.source: Kopf 2023; attribute model trained on HelpSteer and OASST

datasets.name: Domain alignment data
datasets.size: 1,430 samples (design knowledge 302, EDA scripts 480, bug summarization 648)
datasets.source: written by subject matter experts; single-turn QA

datasets.name: Retriever training set
datasets.source: passages from internal design docs; queries generated by Vicuna; hard negatives from Sentence Transformer, positives filtered by Vicuna

datasets.name: Domain AutoEval multiple-choice (Design 94, Scripting 74, Bugs 70, Circuits 227 questions)
datasets.split: 5-shot, mean of 5 runs with varied shots

datasets.name: Chatbot RAG benchmark
datasets.size: 88 questions (Specs, Testbench, Build) over 1.8K documents / 67K passages of ~512 chars

datasets.name: EDA script benchmarks
datasets.size: Python: 146 easy, 28 medium, 25 hard; Tcl: 708 easy, 27 medium, 25 hard

datasets.name: MMLU, Winogrande, hellaswag, ARC-easy, RACE-High, HumanEval, VerilogEval

models.name: ChipNeMo foundation (DAPT)
models.tokenizer: LLaMA2 tokenizer + ~9K domain tokens (new embeddings = mean of sub-token embeddings; output weights zero)

models.name: ChipNeMo chat variants (SFT, SFTG, Steer, SteerG)

other.use: query generation and positive filtering for retriever data

training.objective: autoregressive LM for DAPT; SFT/SteerLM with system and user tokens masked, answer-only loss
training.optimizer: distributed fused Adam, betas 0.9/0.95 (0.9/0.98 for SFT/SteerLM)
training.epochs: SFT 1 epoch; SteerLM 2 epochs; domain data DAPT blend 2-4 epochs
training.hardware: 128 A100 GPUs; NVIDIA NeMo framework with tensor parallelism and flash attention

other.larger_lr_ablation: 3e-4 peak, CosineAnnealing, 200 warmup, min lr 1e-5, batch 256
other.lora_ablation: 26.4M and 211.2M adapters on 13B, single combined QKV low-rank projection per attention layer; rank not stated

inference.decoding: greedy for code benchmarks; temperature=0 single generation for human-scored hard EDA tasks
inference.samples: Pass@5 for automatic EDA; 5 runs with varied 5-shot examples for AutoEval; single generation for human-scored
inference.retrieval: top 8 passages from ~67K passages of ~512 chars; domain-adapted e5 small; for EDA scripts, retrieved API descriptions

metrics.name: Human Likert
metrics.definition: expert rating of chatbot answers and bug summaries

metrics.name: EDA Pass@5
metrics.definition: automatic pass against golden response or code execution

metrics.name: Retrieval hit rate
metrics.definition: whether retrieved passages include the ideal context paragraph

metrics.name: Tokenization efficiency
metrics.definition: token count reduction on domain data

eval.protocol: Human evaluators on Likert scale (number of raters not stated); no significance tests; AutoEval mean of 5 runs without reported variance

limits: Data, benchmarks and tools are proprietary NVIDIA internal; nothing reproducible externally
Benchmarks are small (25 hard tasks per tool, 30 bugs, 88 chat questions); no variance or significance tests; number and calibration of human raters not reported
Authors concede SteerLM with domain data degraded the model's responses in one comparison and attribute it to labeling mismatch (App A.9)
RAG hurt Hard EDA script generation; retrieval for code is under-explored
DAPT 7B slightly degrades open-domain MMLU; authors attribute it to domain data
Triage application left for future work; baselines are LLaMA2 (2023) and GPT-4 of that time
Uses SFT and SteerLM, not RLHF; relevance to RL section is only as an alignment alternative
